For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y(a)=c, the increment in y using the Runge-Kutta Method with step size Δx is computed as the weighted average of four sample slopes: Δy=16(y′+2y1′+2y2′+y3′)⋅Δx, where

  • y′=f(x,y) is the slope at the initial point (x,y),

  • y1′=f(x1,y1) is the slope at (x1,y1)=(x+12Δx,y+12y′⋅Δx),

  • y2′=f(x2,y2) is the slope at (x2,y2)=(x+12Δx,y+12y1′⋅Δx),

  • y3′=f(x3,y3) is the slope at (x3,y3)=(x+Δx,y+y2′⋅Δx).

Since we want to find the value of y at x=0, we will use a step size of Δx=0−(−1)=1.

First, we create a table and add the initial condition data.

x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
−1 1

Now let's find the required values.

  • First, we compute the value of y′ according to the given rule: y′=y(x+1)=1(−1+1)⋅1=0. So, we add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    −1 1 0

  • The first intermediate point is (x1,y1)=(x+12Δx,y+12y′⋅Δx)=(−1+12⋅1,1+12⋅0⋅1)=(−12,1). So, the first intermediate slope is y1′=y1(x1+1)=1⋅(−12+1)=12. We can add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    −1 1 0 12

  • The second intermediate point is (x2,y2)=(x+12Δx,y+12y1′⋅Δx)=(−1+12⋅1,1+12⋅12⋅1)=(−12,54). So, the second intermediate slope is y2′=y2(x2+1)=54⋅(−12+1)=58. We add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    −1 1 0 12 58

  • The third intermediate point is (x3,y3)=(x+Δx,y+y2′⋅Δx)=(−1+1,1+58⋅1)=(0,138). So, the third intermediate slope is y3′=y3(x3+1)=138⋅(0+1)=138. We can add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    −1 1 0 12 58 138

  • Finally, we compute Δy using the Runge-Kutta Method: Δy=16(y′+2y1′+2y2′+y3′)⋅Δx=16(0+2⋅12+2⋅58+138)⋅1=16⋅318=3148. We add this to our table.

    x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
    −1 1 0 12 58 138 3148

To get the values of x and y in the next row, we add Δx to x and Δy to y, as follows:

xnew=x+Δx=−1+1=0ynew=y+Δy=1+3148=7948

Adding these rows to our table gives the following:

x y y′ y1′ y2′ y3′ Δy
−1 1 0 12 58 138 3148
0 7948

Therefore, we conclude that y(0)≈7948.
